children: Shares of Amber Enterprises India rallied as much as 14 percent on Friday, November 13, even as the company reported a mixed set of earnings for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2 FY27). While the company's revenue growth significantly exceeded expectations, driven by strong performance in its electronics division, the losses widened and margins came in sharply below estimates, weighed down by weakness in the consumer durables segment.

Amber Enterprises shares opened at Rs 6,050 and surged 14.19 percent to touch an intra-day high of Rs 6,909, on the BSE. At around 12 pm, the stock pared some of its early gains and was trading 9.13 percent higher at Rs 6782.70.

Amber Enterprises reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 66 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared with a loss of Rs 32 crore in the year-ago period. The loss was also higher than estimate of Rs 57 crore.

The company’s revenue from operations, however, reported a growth of 60 percent year-on-year to Rs 2,627 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with the estimate of 19 percent growth. It stood at Rs 1,647 crore in the year-ago period.
The electronics division emerged as the key growth driver, with revenue jumping 94 percent YoY, against the expected growth of 30 percent.
At the operating level, EBITDA increased 30 percent YoY to Rs 127 crore in the September quarter from Rs 98 crore in the corresponding period last year.

The company attributed the margin pressure particularly in the consumer durables division to commodity inflation, currency fluctuations, minimum wage revisions and expenses associated with its new manufacturing facility at Sri City, which is currently in the ramp-up phase.
Gross margin also declined 200 basis points year-on-year to 19 percent.
Amber Enterprises FY27 outlook: Revenue growth, margin guidance
On the outlook, Amber Enterprises expects FY27 revenue growth to be around 15-20 percent, with performance partly impacted by project delays.
On profitability, the company expects margins to rebound to normalized levels in FY28, supported by the completion and delivery of older projects.

The company expects its consumer durables division to deliver revenue growth broadly in line with the room air conditioner (RAC) industry's growth. However, margins in the segment are likely to remain under pressure, with an estimated full-year impact of 50-100 basis points.
The railway sub-systems business is expected to register revenue growth of around 15-20% in FY27.

Shares of Amber Enterprises have gained over 15 percent in the past two weeks while they have surged 2.24 percent in one month. However, the stock has plunged over 5 percent in three month and 18 percent in six months. On year-to-date basis, the stock is up 5.28 percent, according to BSE analytics.
